summary: Created an LVM logical volume (vgdata/lvdata) on node1, backed by two loopback-file physical volumes since no spare block device existed, formatted ext4 and mounted it at /srv/data. Wrote test data, then grew the LV online (while mounted) from ~1000MiB to ~2.15GiB via vgextend + lvextend + resize2fs, verifying data integrity throughout. Set up persistence across reboot via a systemd oneshot unit (lvm-loopback.service) that reattaches the loop devices and activates the VG before local-fs-pre.target, referenced from /etc/fstab via x-systemd.requires. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id and healthy mount/data state, issued systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified /srv/data remounted automatically at 2.1G with both test files passing sha256sum verification.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout: single 20G vda fully allocated to root/boot, no spare block device or partition available for a native PV
Created two 1200M backing files under /var/lib/lvmfiles and attached them as /dev/loop20 and /dev/loop21
pvcreate on loop20, vgcreate vgdata, lvcreate lvdata (1000M), mkfs.ext4, mounted at /srv/data
Wrote testfile.txt and bigfile.txt to /srv/data and recorded sha256 checksums
pvcreate on loop21, vgextend vgdata with loop21, lvextend +1200M, resize2fs run online while filesystem stayed mounted; final size <2.15GiB / 2.1G reported by df
Verified checksums matched post-extend and confirmed LV remained mounted read-write
Created /etc/systemd/system/lvm-loopback.service (oneshot; reattaches both loop devices, runs udevadm settle, vgchange -ay vgdata before local-fs-pre.target) and enabled it

Simulated boot-time reassembly by unmounting, deactivating the VG, and detaching the loop devices, then starting the service + mount -a; fixed an incorrect /sbin/udevadm path in the unit during this test; confirmed clean automatic reassembly with intact data
Captured pre-reboot boot_id (92ec88af...) and confirmed healthy mount, size, and checksums
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1; connection dropped confirming the command was accepted before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id (2d40a3de...), proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-reboot: /srv/data auto-mounted via the new systemd unit + fstab, size 2.1G (>=2GB), lvm-loopback.service active, and both test files passed sha256sum verification

evidence.summary: df -h shows /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata mounted at /srv/data after lvcreate/mkfs/mount

evidence.requirement: LV grown to >=2GB while staying mounted
evidence.summary: vgextend + lvextend + online resize2fs performed while /srv/data was mounted; lvextend reports growth to <2.15 GiB and df shows 2.1G on /srv/data still mounted

evidence.requirement: Contents stay intact through the extend
evidence.summary: sha256 checksums of testfile.txt and bigfile.txt recorded before extend and verified OK immediately after the online resize

systemd lvm-loopback.service enabled, fstab entry added referencing it, and a simulated teardown/reassembly (detach loops, deactivate VG, restart service, mount -a) proved the automatic reassembly logic works with data intact
Captured boot_id 92ec88af..., confirmed /srv/data mounted at 2.1G, and sha256sum -c passed for both test files before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement / command accepted before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued; exec stream closed as the node went down, confirming the reboot command was accepted

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: First poll failed with connection reset (node down); subsequent poll succeeded returning new boot_id 2d40a3de..., different from the pre-reboot 92ec88af...

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service/data (LV auto-mount, data integrity, cluster membership n/a single node)
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-mounted via lvm-loopback.service (active) at 2.1G, lvs shows lvdata at <2.15g, and sha256sum -c confirmed both test files intact
